title: Three Mile Island Unit 2: partial meltdown, instrumentation ambiguity, and operating-experience correction
summary: TMI-2 is encoded as a severe-accident/correction-memory record about instrumentation ambiguity, human factors, design/operation interfaces, and post-accident operating-experience reform. It is not encoded as a simple operator-error story or a generalized verdict on nuclear power.

status_history.note: Opened nuclear safety design-basis / OPEX lane with official NRC source.

place.location: Three Mile Island Unit 2, near Middletown, Pennsylvania, United States

claims.claim: The NRC backgrounder describes the 28 March 1979 Three Mile Island Unit 2 event as a partial meltdown and the most serious accident in U.S. commercial nuclear power plant operating history; it also says radioactive releases were small with no detectable health effects and attributes the partial meltdown to equipment malfunctions, design-related problems, and worker errors.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The TMI event chain preserved here includes feedwater-pump failure, a pilot-operated relief valve that stuck open, control-room indication that suggested the valve was closed, inadequate or misleading information including no direct indication of core water level, and operator actions taken without awareness of the loss-of-coolant condition.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NRC page says the aftermath brought sweeping changes across emergency response planning, operator training, human factors, radiation protection, design/equipment requirements, resident inspection, risk assessment, enforcement, INPO, problem identification, and operating-experience sharing.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: For the cube, TMI is a correction-history record: a severe event revealed gaps in instrumentation, procedures, human factors, and operating-experience systems, then created explicit correction surfaces whose actual infusion still requires separate child records.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

evidence_refs.support_type: correction memory versus correction infusion pattern

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass official regulator backgrounder extraction; NUREG/Kemeny full report extraction deferred
limitations: Health effects and decommissioning are not fully encoded.

type_payload.system: pressurized water reactor / control room / emergency operating and correction system
sequence_of_events: Pilot-operated relief valve stuck open while indication suggested closed.
Inadequate/misleading information and no direct core-water-level indication impaired diagnosis.
Core overheated and partially melted; post-accident reforms created major correction surfaces.
type_payload.proximate_cause: loss-of-coolant pathway and misdiagnosed plant state during an upset
latent_conditions: control-room instruments did not make key state directly legible
operating-experience sharing was not yet strong enough as a prevention surface

handling_notes: Preserve community harm and worker/family dignity; do not use nuclear accidents as spectacle.
Avoid reducing complex sociotechnical accidents to operator error or using records as blanket ideological claims about nuclear energy.

unknowns: Kemeny Commission, Rogovin, NUREG, and recommendation-status records remain source-acquisition work.

Health-effect and cleanup/decommissioning consequences are intentionally out of scope in this first record.
